grid.title: Enter answers from paper or hand-raising
grid.help: Type the option letter for each question (a, b, c…). Add s, u or g for how sure the student was (bs = B, sure). Type ? if the answer is unreadable, or leave blank if they skipped it. Empty rows are skipped. Saved students are locked, so check before saving.

drafts.title: AI drafts and review
drafts.intro: The AI can draft questions and explanations. Everything it writes starts as a draft that only you can see. Our code checks what it can, you read the rest, and nothing reaches students until you approve it.
drafts.aiOff: AI drafting is turned off or not set up. You can still review drafts you already have. Everything else in Adhyaapak works as normal.
drafts.slotsLeft_one: {{count}} more draft allowed until you review some
drafts.slotsLeft_other: {{count}} more drafts allowed until you review some
drafts.discardedNote: Discarded drafts are not saved. Asking again is fine.
drafts.badge: AI draft: not visible to students until you approve it
drafts.verified: Our code checked the arithmetic and the wrong-answer patterns, and they are correct.
drafts.failed: Our checks found a problem. Fix it, or reject this draft.
drafts.notCheckedHelp: Read the answer and every option yourself before approving.
drafts.optionsLegend: Options (choose the correct one, and what each wrong answer shows)
drafts.iChecked: I read the answer and every option and they are correct.
drafts.iReadIt: I read this explanation and it is correct.

syllabus.title: Syllabus to concept graph
syllabus.intro: Upload or paste one chapter or unit of a syllabus. The AI proposes which concepts it covers and which come first. You review every prerequisite the document does not back up, and nothing becomes part of your curriculum until you publish it.
syllabus.limits: PDF, .txt or .md. One chapter or unit at a time (about 24,000 characters, 60 pages). Scanned PDFs cannot be read: paste the text instead.
syllabus.alreadyUploaded: You already added this exact text, so the existing copy is shown.
syllabus.suspicious: This document contains wording that looks like instructions to an AI. It was treated as plain text and never obeyed, but it is worth a look.
syllabus.subject: Subject
syllabus.takesAMoment: This can take up to a minute.
syllabus.reviewIntro: Review everything below. Prerequisites the document does not state are marked and need your decision.
syllabus.legend: Boxes are concepts, drawn left to right in teaching order. A dashed outline means the document never mentions the concept. Solid arrows are accepted prerequisites; dashed arrows marked ? are waiting for you.
syllabus.pictureLabel: Concept graph with {{count}} concepts. The list below describes every prerequisite.
syllabus.noPrereqs: No prerequisites were proposed. You can add them below.
syllabus.notInDocHelp: The AI inferred this from general subject knowledge, so check that it is right for your syllabus.
syllabus.conceptNotQuoted: No passage in the document could be matched to this concept.
syllabus.publishWarning: Publishing creates a new curriculum version. It is added for every teacher on this installation and does not replace anything that exists.
syllabus.confirmPublish: I have reviewed the concepts and prerequisites and want to publish this curriculum.
syllabus.published: Published as version {{version}}: {{concepts}} concepts and {{edges}} prerequisites.
syllabus.nextSteps: The new concepts have no questions yet. Open a concept and use AI drafts and review to create some, or add them another way, before running a diagnostic.

paper.title: Paper answer sheets
paper.intro: Students answer on paper. You photograph each sheet, check what was read against the photo, and approve it. Only approved sheets become part of the learning record.
paper.tipPhoto: Photograph the sheet flat, in good light, with all the answer boxes in view. JPEG or PNG.
paper.tipNames: Ask students not to write their name on the sheet: the photo may be sent to an AI service to be read.
paper.tipPrivate: Photos are private to you. Location and camera details are removed, and each photo is deleted after a retention period once approved.
paper.printLink: Print answer sheets with boxes (easier to read than free handwriting)
paper.notStarted: Start the activity (or finish it) before adding paper sheets.
paper.everyoneDone: Every student already has an answer or a sheet waiting.
paper.uploaded: Photo added. Open it to review.
paper.accuracy: So far the reader got {{answers}} answers from {{sheets}} sheets and you changed {{changed}} of them.
paper.approvedMsg: Approved. These answers are now part of the learning record.
paper.rejectedMsg: This sheet was rejected and its photo was deleted. It has not affected anyone's record.
paper.photoGone: The photo has been deleted, so this sheet can no longer be checked.
paper.stripped: Location and camera details were removed from this photo.
paper.deleteAfter: Kept until about {{date}}, then deleted automatically.
paper.readIntro: Let the AI read the sheet to save typing, or choose the answers yourself from the photo.
paper.consent: I understand this photo will be sent to the AI service to be read, and it has no student names on it.
paper.aiOff: AI reading is switched off. Choose the answers yourself from the photo.
paper.readFailed: The AI could not read this photo. Choose the answers yourself from the photo.
paper.readBy: Read by {{who}} ({{version}}). It only reads; it does not mark anything.
paper.notRead: Not read yet. Choose from the photo.
paper.approve: Approve and add to the learning record
paper.approveHelp: “Can't read” and “blank” count as no evidence, not as wrong. Nothing is added to the learning record until you approve.
paper.saved: Saved. You can come back and approve it later.
paper.chooseAll: Choose an answer for every question first.
paper.printIntro: One sheet for each of the {{count}} students who have not answered yet. Sheets show the roll number, not the name.
paper.sheetRule: Write one letter in each box. Please do not write your name on this sheet.
paper.readerCouldNot: The reader could not tell what was marked.

offline.title: Offline lesson packs
offline.intro: Prepare a lesson while you are connected. A pack holds the explanations, a short check, printable sheets and your class's roll numbers, so you can teach and record answers with no internet. Sync afterwards to save your records.
offline.offlineNow: Offline: work is saved on this device
offline.noPacks: No packs yet. Open a lesson and choose “Prepare for offline use”.
offline.removeConfirm: Remove this pack from this device? Answers already recorded stay in the sync queue.
offline.ready: Pack ready: {{count}} items saved on this device
offline.privacy: Packs hold roll numbers only (no names). Answer keys are only used to print the teacher's key.
offline.packMissing: This pack is not saved on this device.
offline.printPack: Print worksheet, response sheet and key
offline.recordHelp: Choose each student's answers from the paper responses, then press Record. It is saved on this device and sent when you are connected. Marking happens after syncing.
offline.recordNote: Left empty means no answer, which counts as no evidence, never as wrong.
offline.printIntro: Print everything now, even with no connection. The answer key prints on its own page.
offline.responseHelp: Write each student's letter in the box. Enter them into the app later.
offline.syncLater: Later: open the app, choose this pack and record these answers, then sync.
offline.keyWarning: Teacher only. Do not hand this page to students.

brief.title: Tomorrow's teaching brief
brief.intro: A short summary built only from the answers recorded for this class. Lines marked “from records” are counts you can check on the learning map. Suggestions say which counts they rest on. Accept, reword or dismiss each one.
brief.footer: Counts come from the evidence recorded so far and may change as more answers arrive. Misconception patterns are provisional.
brief.basis_one: Based on {{answersRecorded}} recorded answers from {{students}} students, across {{count}} concept.
brief.basis_other: Based on {{answersRecorded}} recorded answers from {{students}} students, across {{count}} concepts.

atlas.title: Misconception Atlas
atlas.intro: Known error patterns for each concept, what a typical wrong answer looks like, and what to do about it. The counts are from your own classes only. They show how often your confirmations have supported a pattern; they do not prove a pattern is scientifically valid.

quality.often_rejected: Often rejected: consider whether this pattern fits your students

textbook.title: Class 6 Mathematics textbook
textbook.lede: Our own textbook, written for Adhyaapak and organised in teaching order. Each chapter has a short summary, the key ideas to land, and its lessons. Your timetable plans these lessons for you.
textbook.provenance: Written by the Adhyaapak team. Topics follow the usual Class 6 syllabus; the wording is ours, not copied from any book.
textbook.ownSyllabusBody: You can upload your own syllabus and review a concept graph made from it. Most teachers will not need this.
